data.exact_reserve_text: The 2017 year has closed with a deficit of GBP 12.6m which equates to a loss of 9.8% on stamp capacity. The result is driven by reserve increases in the closed years, where the 2013 and 2016 years have required reserve strengthening beyond their respective pure year close position. In contrast the 2014 and 2015 years are performing better than expected when those years were closed. Unfavourable development for 2016 is particularly disappointing and is driven by catastrophe losses, strengthening of liability reserves and a deterioration in Specialty loss ratios. This development further supports the remediation actions taken in subsequent years. The result for the account has been impacted by the movement in large claim reserves for the 2013 and 2014 years, and late development of certain claims from the 2015 year, as well as an adjustment to reserves on certain more specialised business. For the 2016 year, catastrophe losses, liability reserve increases and Specialty class loss ratio deterioration have specifically contributed to the loss.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a significant gross reserve strengthening of GBP 58.42 million for prior underwriting years (2013-2017). This adverse development was primarily driven by reserve increases for the 2013 and 2016 years, including catastrophe losses, liability reserve increases, and deterioration in Specialty loss ratios for 2016. There was also late development of claims from 2015 and adjustments to reserves for specialised business. Partially offsetting this were favourable developments on the 2014 and 2015 years, which performed better than expected.
